title: Evaluation of towers has an exact right adjoint
statement:
For $n\geq1$ and an $\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$-module sheaf $J$ on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$,
let $r_nJ\in\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ be the tower with $(r_nJ)_r=J$ for
$r\geq n$ (an $\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^r$-module by restriction of scalars along
$\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^r\to\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$), $(r_nJ)_r=0$ for $r<n$,
identity transitions $(r_nJ)_{r+1}\to(r_nJ)_r$ for $r\geq n$ and zero
transitions below. Then $r_n$ is an exact functor, right adjoint to evaluation
$C_\bullet\mapsto C_n$. Consequently $r_n$ preserves injective objects, and
every tower $C_\bullet$ embeds into $\prod_{n\geq1}r_nJ_n$ for injective
$\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$-modules $J_n\supset C_n$.

proof.text: Use the normalized right-adjoint construction, whose fields fix every upper/lower level, transition and map. Copy these fields into the original interface.
Right adjoints preserve all limits, hence finite limits. The separate levelwise finite-colimit theorem gives the other half of exactness.
Install A.evaluationLimits and apply Adjunction.preservesInjectiveObjects_of_preservesFiniteLimits to each evaluation adjunction.

Apply the common-universe ring-sheaf Grothendieck theorem to each level and the enough-injectives theorem to obtain J_n and mono i_n. A.grothendieck gives products of towers. Form the limiting fan and Pi.lift of the adjunct maps. To prove the lift mono, an equality after it gives equality after each adjunct by projecting. Naturality and injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence give equality after i_n, and its monicity gives equality of evaluations. The normalized equivalence is faithful and strict-system maps are determined componentwise, so the original maps are equal. Pi.lift_π gives the required component formula. No levelwise product computation or explicit finite product tower is required.
